NDT training in Las Vegas: how it works for Las Vegas employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT trains Las Vegas technicians to ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Theory runs live online or onsite at your facility in the valley, practical work is done on real specimens under an ASNT Level III, and your employer certifies you under its written practice. Atlantis has no Las Vegas classroom; the training is delivered to you.

Southern Nevada is a construction-and-power market, not a refinery market, and that shapes what training makes sense. Most local NDT work is structural weld inspection on steel buildings, arenas, data centres and transmission structures, plus maintenance inspection at generating stations, solar plants and federal sites. Those jobs lean heavily on VT, MT and UT to AWS D1.1, with RT on piping and pressure work. This section explains which courses map to that work, how certification actually happens under SNT-TC-1A, how Nevada regulates radiography crews, what local training options exist, and the questions Las Vegas technicians ask most.

Know what you need already? Request a Las Vegas training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Las Vegas

All courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and are written to fit inside your company's written practice. Level I and II courses cover principles, equipment, technique, procedures and code acceptance criteria; Level III preparation covers the Basic and method exams.

MethodLevelsWhat Las Vegas employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic, shear wave and thickness)I, II, III prepComplete-joint-penetration groove welds in structural steel moment frames; thickness checks on plant piping and tanksNone for Level I; Level I time and hours for Level II under your written practice
PAUT (phased array UT)II, III prepFaster, recorded weld inspection on large structural and power projects; alternative to RT where shutting down a site for radiation is impracticalUT Level II or equivalent UT background
TOFDIIFlaw sizing on thick welds in pressure equipment and heavy fabricationUT Level II
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepPipe weld radiography on gas lines, plant piping and pressure equipment; digital and film interpretationRadiation safety training and radiographer certification before working as a radiographer (see licensing below)
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, III prepFillet and groove weld surface inspection on erected steel; lifting equipment; rotating plant equipmentNone for Level I
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, III prepStainless and aluminium welds, castings and non-magnetic components; aviation partsNone for Level I
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepWeld size, profile and workmanship checks that underpin every structural inspection; corrosion surveysNone for Level I
ET (eddy current)I, II, III prepAircraft structure and wheel inspection; heat-exchanger and condenser tubing at generating stationsNone for Level I

Hours by method and level are listed in the SNT-TC-1A training requirements matrix. We link to it instead of printing hour counts here because your written practice can require more than the recommended minimum, and auditors check your document, not ours.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Las Vegas, step by step

Under SNT-TC-1A, a training course does not certify you. Your employer does. The path looks like this:

  1. Written practice. Your employer's document sets the training, experience, exam and vision requirements. No written practice, no valid certification; a Level III can write one for you.
  2. Classroom training in the method and level, live online or onsite in Las Vegas.
  3. On-the-job experience under supervision, logged and signed.
  4. General exam on method principles.
  5. Specific exam on your employer's procedures, equipment and the codes you inspect to, such as AWS D1.1.
  6. Practical exam on real flawed specimens, administered under an ASNT Level III.
  7. Vision test, near-vision acuity and colour contrast, renewed every year.
  8. Employer certification, signed by the responsible Level III and the employer.
  9. Recertification at the interval and by the method your written practice specifies.

The hours for steps 2 and 3 are in the requirements matrix. For the full background see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Las Vegas crews

  • Live online theory plus onsite practical. Classroom sessions run live in Pacific time. The practical then happens at your shop, yard or plant in Clark County using your equipment and specimens, or specimens we provide.
  • Fully onsite cohort. For crews of several technicians, the Level III runs theory and practical at your facility. This also works for sites outside the valley, including Henderson, North Las Vegas, Pahrump, Mesquite and the solar fields along US-95.
  • Individual online enrolment. A single technician takes theory through NDT training online, then completes the practical and exams with their employer's Level III.

Las Vegas scheduling is driven by project phases rather than refinery turnarounds. Structural inspection demand peaks when steel erection starts on a big project, and the summer heat changes how practical sessions are run outdoors. Many employers train during the design and foundation phases so Level IIs are certified before the first steel arrives. Give us the project dates and we plan backwards. Ask about onsite training for your Las Vegas crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Las Vegas

Structural steel and special inspection

The resort corridor, arenas, stadiums, hospitals, warehouses and the valley's growing data-centre campuses all use structural steel that needs weld inspection. The governing code is usually AWS D1.1, and building-code special inspection in Clark County and the cities of Las Vegas, Henderson and North Las Vegas requires inspectors approved under the local special-inspection programme. Those approvals often call for AWS CWI or ICC credentials as well as ASNT Level II for UT and MT. Atlantis trains the ASNT side; we mention CWI and ICC only as context for what local employers ask for.

Power generation and renewables

Gas-fired generating stations in the valley, Hoover Dam's hydropower plant, utility-scale solar and battery storage, and high-voltage transmission lines all need maintenance inspection. Typical work includes UT thickness and weld inspection on piping to ASME B31.1, ET on condenser and heat-exchanger tubes, and MT and VT on structural supports.

Pipelines and gas distribution

Natural gas transmission and distribution lines serving Southern Nevada, and fuel pipelines feeding the airport and terminals, use welding and NDT to API 1104 and federal pipeline rules. RT and, increasingly, automated UT are the standard methods.

Federal, defense and aviation

Nellis Air Force Base, Creech Air Force Base and the Nevada National Security Site bring defense work with security and base-access requirements on top of technical qualification. Harry Reid International Airport and general-aviation maintenance shops need PT, ET and UT on aircraft components; aerospace work often follows NAS 410, which we note as context only.

Mining and heavy equipment

Nevada's mining industry, mostly in the north of the state, relies on MT and UT for crack detection on haul trucks, shovels and crusher components. Las Vegas-based technicians sometimes rotate to those sites.

Radiography licensing in Nevada

Nevada is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials licences, including industrial radiography with Ir-192 sources, are issued and inspected by the Radiation Control Program in the Nevada Division of Public and Behavioral Health, which also registers X-ray machines. Out-of-state radiography firms must obtain reciprocity before working in Nevada. Under the Agreement State equivalent of 10 CFR Part 34, each radiographer needs radiographer certification from a recognised certifying entity plus the licensee's radiation safety training. Our RT courses teach the NDT method; they are not a radiation licence, and the Radiation Safety Officer remains responsible for compliance.

TWIC and site access

Las Vegas has no seaport, so TWIC rarely applies locally. It becomes relevant if you travel to work on port or marine terminal projects in California. Federal sites such as Nellis and the Nevada National Security Site require their own access processing, sometimes including a security clearance.

Method spotlight: UT of structural groove welds to AWS D1.1

The most valuable single skill for a Las Vegas technician is ultrasonic inspection of complete-joint-penetration groove welds in structural steel. AWS D1.1 sets a specific ultrasonic procedure: calibrated shear-wave angle beams, defined scanning patterns, decibel-based flaw rating, and acceptance tables that differ for statically and cyclically loaded connections. A technician who understands how the code calculates an indication rating, how to handle backing bars and weld access holes, and how to report so the engineer of record can act, is in demand on every large project in the valley. Our UT Level II course works through these D1.1 scenarios in detail, and teams that already hold UT Level II can move on to PAUT for structural welds, which some engineers now accept as an alternative where the project specification allows.

Local options compared: NDT training in and around Las Vegas

  • College of Southern Nevada (CSN). Runs a welding technology programme with entry-level and advanced certificates and an associate degree, including SMAW, GMAW, FCAW and GTAW and blueprint reading. It is a strong route into welding and a good foundation for later inspection work. It is not an ASNT NDT certification course.
  • Local inspection firms and special-inspection agencies. Several Las Vegas companies train their own staff in-house under their own written practices. If you are hired by one of them, their programme is your certification route.
  • ASNT local section. We could not confirm an ASNT section based in Las Vegas; use the ASNT section directory to find the nearest one. ASNT's annual conference has been held in Las Vegas, which is a useful networking opportunity when it returns.
  • Out-of-state schoolhouses. Open-enrolment NDT schools in California, Arizona and Texas run scheduled courses. Good for one person at a time; travel and lodging add up for a crew.
  • Atlantis NDT. No Las Vegas centre. Live online theory and onsite cohorts at your facility under an ASNT Level III, with written-practice development and Level III exam services for employers. Best fit: Las Vegas employers qualifying a crew, and technicians whose employer will certify them.

Level III services and written practices for Las Vegas NDT companies

Many Southern Nevada inspection firms are special-inspection agencies whose technicians do NDT alongside other inspections. Their certification files are often the weak point in a client audit. Atlantis supports them with written practice development and review (written practice development), Level III examination services, procedure writing for AWS D1.1 and ASME work, and crew-wide corporate NDT training.

For consulting see NDT consulting in Nevada and our steel and structural NDT consulting page for Las Vegas. For the statewide training view see NDT training across Nevada. Book a Level III consultation if you need a written practice or procedure before your next audit.

What a Las Vegas employer receives at the end of a cohort

Training only helps you in an audit if the paperwork matches your written practice. At the end of an Atlantis cohort the employer receives an attendance and classroom-hours record for each trainee, the graded general, specific and practical examination records, vision test documentation where we administered it, and a certification packet laid out to match the employer's own written practice so the Level III of record and the employer can sign. Where the employer's written practice is out of date, for example still referencing an older SNT-TC-1A edition or missing a method the crew now performs, we flag it before the cohort starts rather than after. For special-inspection agencies, that packet is usually what a building official, general contractor or engineer of record asks to see when they question a technician's qualification on a structural project.

Individual technician or company team?

If you are an individual in Las Vegas looking to break into NDT, the quickest path is usually to get hired as a trainee by an inspection firm or fabricator and let the employer sponsor your training and certification, because certification under SNT-TC-1A always runs through an employer. If you are a company, a single cohort for your whole crew keeps everybody on one written practice and one set of records, which is easier to defend in an audit than a mix of certificates from different schools.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. The welding workshop scene is closest to Las Vegas structural work, and the hangar scene suits aviation technicians. See also the Las Vegas practical NDT page. The simulator is for practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who sets course content, reviews written practices and oversees examinations. Level III candidates should see ASNT Level III training.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Las Vegas

How do I get NDT certified in Las Vegas?

Take classroom training in a method, build supervised experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams and a vision test, and be certified by your employer under its SNT-TC-1A written practice. Atlantis provides the training and Level III support; the employer issues the certification.

Can I take NDT training online in Nevada?

Theory, yes, live online in Pacific time. The practical and the practical exam must be done hands-on with real specimens at your employer's facility or in an onsite cohort.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the hours set in your written practice and whether you hold UT Level I. The recommended classroom and experience hours are in our training requirements matrix.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Nevada?

Your employer needs a radioactive materials licence from the Nevada Radiation Control Program (or reciprocity if licensed elsewhere), and each radiographer needs recognised radiographer certification and radiation safety training. X-ray machines must be registered with the same programme.

What does NDT training cost in Las Vegas?

We quote on request. The figure depends on method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery and travel. Quotes come back within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Las Vegas employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A employer certification is the norm for UT, MT and RT on structural, power and pipeline work. Many structural employers also ask for AWS CWI, and some local special-inspection programmes want ICC credentials.

Do I need a CWI as well as ASNT Level II?

For structural special inspection in Las Vegas, many employers want both. Atlantis trains the ASNT methods only; CWI is administered by the American Welding Society.

Can you train our crew at our Las Vegas facility?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your shop, yard or plant is the usual model for cohorts, using your procedures and equipment.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA to pay for NDT training?

Those programmes generally require a school or provider approved by the VA or listed by the state. Atlantis does not claim VA or WIOA approval, so ask your VA or Nevada JobConnect counsellor first. Employer-paid training is the usual route for our courses.

Is there an NDT school in Las Vegas?

We could not find an open-enrolment ASNT NDT school based in Las Vegas. CSN offers welding; NDT training locally is usually employer-run, delivered onsite, or taken online.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III in Las Vegas?

Yes, through live online Level III preparation. The ASNT Level III exams themselves are booked through ASNT's testing arrangements.

How should I practise for the practical exam?

Work real specimens under supervision, rehearse on the Practical NDT simulator, and try mock questions such as UT Level 2 practice questions.

What do NDT technicians earn in Nevada?

It varies by method, level and sector. For published ranges, see our NDT salary guide.
